Specification: This module is a test specification designed to check the syntactic and semantic constraints on the use of temporal operators in TLA+. The comments and operator definitions illustrate which uses of primed variables and temporal operators are permitted and which are considered errors. The module does not model a real algorithm or system, but rather serves as a suite of test cases for the TLA+ parser or semantic checker, especially regarding the correct placement and usage of primed variables, temporal formulas, and quantification. No fault model or liveness/safety property is being verified; the focus is on language-level correctness and error detection.

DivisionNotes: Partition count: StatePredicate(0) + TemporalProperty(14) + Init(0) + ValueDef(1) + ActionDefNames(0) = 15 = OperatorDefNames total. Verified.
All operators except m2 have a temporal operator ([] or <> or ~> or -+->) at the outermost or near-outermost level, so are classified as TemporalProperty.

Operator m2 is a value-level definition: m2 == \A i \in x' : x'. It is not a state predicate (contains primed variables), not a temporal property (no temporal operator), not an Init, so is placed in ValueDef by elimination.

TemporalNesting is true: operator a == x ~> []x contains []x nested inside ~> (which is syntactic sugar for [](x => <>y)), but here []x is an argument to ~>. Similarly, operators b, c, d, e, f, m, n, mm, nn all have temporal operators nested inside another temporal operator. Example line: a == x ~> []x
